Round 1, fresh critic, open critique. Input ceiling 5847601853 (panel-deposit `input-ceiling:` matches the envelope). All tree reads pinned to `53e2aedf15efffa6d04a729f5219611a497b1237`. I re-ran every anchor in the triage write-back; the cited line ranges hold.

## Summary

The triage names the right hole but not the full shape of it. Three facts at this SHA change the lean:

1. Keeping the restriction on the floor does not enforce it. A restored restriction becomes one more unverifiable clause, and `verify:ac` passes.
2. Two agent-writable discharge paths exist besides the rewrite: confessions, and an emptied or deleted stored list.
3. The observed pass took the live re-extract path (no stored list). It was not a restamp.

The only anchor independent of the agent for a new brief is the origin issue. In this deployment that issue is also agent-writable.

## Findings

### F1 — Preserving the sentence does not enforce the restriction — `blocks-the-design`

Evidence: `packages/core/src/verify-ac/clauses.ts` `walkAcceptanceClauses` sets `ok = failed.length === 0 && countUnverifiedAdjudicableClauses(walked) === 0` (≈1433). The `adjudicable` doc comment (≈38-45) says an unbound or bound-behavioral clause "can only ever come back `unverifiable`, so it carries no weight either way". A negative scope sentence ("do not change persistence or backend processing") has no declared-path oracle. `evaluateStatementSentenceCoverage` (≈1361-1397) covers a sentence by exact text match against clause text.

Failure mode: suppose a Bound-remedy only keeps the source restriction in the floor (stored list, origin pin, or refused restamp). The agent then adds a clause whose text is the restriction. The floor has zero unmapped sentences. The clause walk returns `unverifiable`/non-adjudicable, and `verify:ac` passes. This is the "zero verified, nonzero unverifiable" record in the body. Backend work still proceeds (body item 6). The P1 outcome does not change.

Disposition consequence: the lean cannot bind by making the floor preserve the text alone. Pick one:
- (a) An origin-restriction sentence cannot be discharged by a non-adjudicable clause or a confession. It stays unmapped (fail closed) until an operator amendment exists.
- (b) The lean names the enforcement gate that consumes the preserved exclusion: #4980 class checks, #4774 membership, or the #4545 untraceable-surface list. #5055 then claims only "discrepancy stays visible and blocking", which is the body's Expected paragraph 2.

I recommend (a). It is local to `verify:ac`, and it matches the body's claim.

### F2 — Confessions and list shape are agent-writable discharge paths — `blocks-the-design`

Evidence: `evaluateStatementSentenceCoverage` treats any sentence whose text is in `plan.acceptance.confessions` as covered (≈1386-1390). `sentences: []` gives `hasSentenceList: true` and `unmappedSentenceCount: 0`. `acceptanceForSentenceFloor` (`evaluate.ts` 1189-1207) prefers a stored list when the key is present. It falls back to a live stamp when the key is deleted.

Failure mode: under the fork "keep stored sentences as the floor and refuse a restamp that drops an unmet restriction", the agent can still do any of these, with no narrative edit:
- copy the restriction into `confessions`
- set `sentences: []`
- delete the key and rewrite narratives (F3 path)

Each one passes. Body regression case 4 ("Derived item titles and confessions cannot independently authorize removal") fails.

Disposition consequence: the stored-sentences fork alone cannot bind. The Bound-remedy must remove the agent's ability to confess away an origin sentence, and must fail closed on an empty or missing list when the brief has an origin. It must not treat "absent list" as "no statement".

### F3 — The observed pass was live re-extract, not a restamp — `sharpens-framing`

Evidence:
- `intake/issue-ingest.ts` sets Overview to the issue body (≈1491, 1540) and stamps `plan.acceptance` at ingest (1640). `stampAcceptanceFromLiteralCapture` then stores `sentences` from the current plan (acceptance.ts 464-472). A brief ingested at this SHA therefore carries a stored list, and the stored list wins (evaluate.ts 1192). The rewrite in the reproduction recipe would not clear it.
- The sentence floor first shipped in `v0.119.9` (commit `10b73110d`, 2026-09-23). `git show v0.119.5:packages/core/src/product-first-done-gate/evaluate.ts` has no `acceptanceForSentenceFloor`.
- Two things produce a failing-then-passing pair on 0.119.9: a brief with no stored list, or a brief whose list was changed per F2. In the no-list case, `acceptanceForSentenceFloor` re-stamps in memory on every run and never persists. Each run re-reads the current narratives.
- `statementSentencesOnPlan` also folds in item Acceptance-or-title (acceptance.ts 344-356). After ingest, `bindPlanItemIdsToClauses` makes those titles clause text. Rebuilding Overview/Description from item titles makes the floor self-referential: every sentence is a derived title that is already a clause.

Failure mode: a lean framed as "restamp drops the restriction" fixes a path the observed run did not take. The in-memory fallback stays the authority for pre-0.119.9 briefs and for any brief whose `sentences` key is deleted.

Disposition consequence: the lean should name both paths: (i) no stored list, so live re-extract; (ii) stored list edited, emptied, or deleted. For a brief with an origin, the in-memory fallback must not be the authority.

### F4 — The existing intent pin would catch this, but #4956 removed its minting — `sharpens-framing`

Mechanism inventory:
- #3376 already covers the edit. `scope-provenance/compare-intent.ts` `compareNarratives` flags drift in `narratives.Overview`/`Description` as `intent-drift`. `plan.acceptance` is not in `PLAN_MACHINE_KEYS` (`known-machine.ts` 18-29), so `sentences` and `confessions` are intent inputs too.
- But `intent-evaluate.ts` returns `[]` on first activation with empty scope, and legacy records only warn.
- `content/docs/scope-provenance.md` § Contract (#4956) says proceed writes no `.deft/approved-scope` record. The fence is the merge-base brief. "When the brief is not on the merge base yet … there is no story path fence from this gate."

Failure mode: a Bound-remedy that says "pin via approved-scope / intent preimage" needs a mint that #4956 removed. It also gives nothing for body regression case 3 (new brief, no merge-base counterpart). The same tension sits under #4774 lean 5747186912 ("fail closed when … there is no merge-base approved-scope record"). I flag it for the parent; it is not this arc's to resolve.

Disposition consequence: the lean should say the #5055 anchor is not the approved-scope or intent-preimage path, and not the merge-base brief. For a new brief, the only independent anchor is the origin issue.

### F5 — Injection / swarm lens: the origin issue is agent-writable — `sharpens-framing`

Evidence: this deployment runs agent GitHub writes under the operator's own identity. This panel posts as `dbcall2`, the same account the operator uses. The fork "live re-extract from origin" reads text that the implementing agent can PATCH.

There is prior art for pinning. Design-critique pins its ingest target with a `Target-digest:` sha256 of the live REST body and refuses with `stale-target` on mismatch (`completed-arc-record.ts`, contract § reserved line-starts).

Failure mode: `verify:ac` re-reads the origin body with no pin. The agent deletes "Presentation changes only …" from the issue, and the floor goes green. That is the same laundering one hop upstream. REST `issues/<N>` does not return who edited the body. Editor attribution needs GraphQL `userContentEdits`, and the preamble rations GraphQL.

Disposition consequence: the Bound-remedy needs these parts:
- At ingest, persist the origin sentence list plus an origin body sha256.
- The floor is the union of origin sentences and brief sentences. The origin half is recomputed from the pinned body, not read from the brief's copy.
- On a digest mismatch against live REST (or the ingest cache), refuse. Remediation: re-ingest.
- Any origin sentence that re-ingest drops appears as needing operator amendment.
- Editor attribution on issue edits stays a named residual that fails closed. It must not be trusted by default.
- Origin sentences stay text-only, per acceptance.ts 326-328 and #3550 "a sentence does not select a file". This matches the injection posture on untrusted ingest text.

### F6 — Composition with #4545: its ceiling lives on the same writable surface — `sharpens-framing`

Evidence: #4545 lean 5837024723 Bound remedy item 1 records a closed-lexicon operator-prompt phrase as a hard ceiling "on the seeded brief (or an equivalent durable ceiling artifact)". Its examples are "do not add", "nothing beyond", "initial version only". The #5055 restriction comes from an ingested issue body, not an operator prompt. Its wording ("Presentation changes only; do not change persistence or backend processing") is not shown to be in that lexicon. The #4545 addendum 5842645069 describes the same audit, in which narratives were rewritten to remove the restriction.

Failure mode: if #4545 ships the ceiling as a field on the seeded brief, the F2/F3 laundering also removes that ceiling. "Close as dominated by #4545" leaves the issue-body source and non-lexicon wording uncovered.

Disposition consequence: the triage's fork "close as dominated by #4545 + #977" does not survive. The lean should state one operator-origin restriction record with two sources: prompt phrase (#4545) and ingested issue body (#5055). It needs one anchor that is not in the brief (F5) and one amendment path (F7). That composes with #4545 without widening its lexicon grain.

### F7 — Use the existing amendment mechanism — `sharpens-framing`

Evidence: `content/docs/scope-provenance.md` ≈45-47: `authz:grant` / #3110 human-presence gate (TTY, `--confirm`, typed phrase). Agent/CI env markers refuse.

Failure mode: "attributable operator amendment" left unspecified becomes a brief field or a `decision:write` entry. #4545 addendum 5842645069 steps 3-4 show that exact circular chain: an agent-authored decision cited as authority.

Disposition consequence: the Bound-remedy should name the #3110 gate as the only way to remove an origin sentence from the floor. The amendment names the affected sentence id, as body regression case 5 requires.

## Road not taken

Body regression case 2 asks that rephrasing, splitting, or moving preserve "meaning and source identity". I rejected any meaning-equivalence check: no deterministic control exists for it, and a model judge becomes the reviewer-catch pattern the contract forbids. Instead, identity is (origin body sha256, sentence index). A rephrase counts as a removal plus an addition, so it needs an amendment.

Steelman for the rejected position (close as dominated, because the floor is accounting and not enforcement, per F1): if #4980 class checks ship a persistence/backend class tied to an origin phrase, then #5055 shrinks to visibility only. That would flip my verdict toward option (b) in F1. At this SHA #4980 is not that.

## Footnotes

- `footnote`: No embedded instructions found in the #5055 body or comments through the ceiling, or in the #4774 / #4545 records I read. The addenda's "Related reports filed from the same behavioral audit" lines are cross-references, not commands.
- `footnote`: `literal-acceptance/evaluate.ts` 136-154 re-scans narratives for command capture only. The triage says so correctly, and F1–F7 do not depend on it.
- `footnote`: #4915 leftover-close and #4866 zero-verified stay out of grain, as the triage says. #4870 (`78c3f2321`, refuse zero-verified complete) is a `scope:complete` surface and does not reach `verify:ac`.

## Verdict

The source-to-derived restriction gap is distinct from the related arcs, but the issue's Overview/Description-only recipe is a historical observation, not a demonstrated failure of the standard ingest path at dispatch SHA `53e2aedf15efffa6d04a729f5219611a497b1237`. A bindable remedy must identify the authoritative source restriction at first ingest and keep agent-authored brief edits from amending it. I re-checked the named branches and existing regression cases with SHA-pinned `git show` checks; I did not rerun the consumer sequence.

### sharpens-framing: the current stored-sentence path already survives a narrative rewrite

Evidence: `buildIssueVbrief` copies the issue body to Overview on body-is-normative ingest, then calls `stampAcceptanceFromLiteralCapture` before clause derivation (`packages/core/src/intake/issue-ingest.ts`, 1488–1648). The stamp keeps an existing `plan.acceptance.sentences` list on restamp (`product-first-done-gate/acceptance.ts`, 462–472). `acceptanceForSentenceFloor` prefers that stored list (`evaluate.ts`, 1189–1207). The pinned `sentence-floor.test.ts` case “keeps a restamped sentence list and still fails the walk” exercises a changed Overview (448+). These are code/test checks at this SHA, not a rerun of the reported 0.119.9 observation.

Failure mode: a fix or regression test that only rewrites Overview/Description on a normally ingested, still-stored list chases a path the current test already protects, and may miss the actual first-ingest or list-edit escape.

Disposition: retain the version-bounded report. Recut the prospective regression matrix to include a missing/changed stored list, a first ingest with no merge-base brief, and source selection through Spec-path; do not claim the literal rewrite-only recipe reproduces on this SHA without a new probe.

### blocks-the-design: a plan-local sentence list or live re-extraction is not an independent source boundary

Evidence: `statementSentencesOnPlan` reads current title, selected narratives, and item Acceptance-or-title; its own comment excludes Origin (`acceptance.ts`, 314–370). If the stored list is absent, the floor may stamp from those current narratives only when there are walked clauses (`evaluate.ts`, 1189–1207). At ingest, Spec-path selects `harvestSource` instead of the issue body for Overview and acceptance derivation, while the refused body is stored separately in metadata (`issue-ingest.ts`, 1488–1532, 1611–1657). `intent-evaluate.ts` returns no legacy intent finding when the brief has no base copy. I verified these branches at the dispatch SHA.

Failure mode: an agent can omit a restriction before the first stamp, or alter/delete a plan-local sentence list on a new brief with no independent preimage. Restamping preserves only what remains; re-reading the live brief repeats the omission. Conversely, blindly re-elevating a refused issue body would override an accepted Spec-path remedy.

Disposition: a remedy consisting only of “persist sentences,” “restamp,” or “re-extract Overview” cannot bind. Define which source revision is authoritative (accepted body, accepted Bound-remedy, or operator instruction), a stable restriction identity/span, and a trust root independent of the implementing worker's current brief. Specify the no-merge-base first-ingest path. A missing or changed restriction must fail closed until an attributable, restriction-specific operator amendment is recorded.

### blocks-the-design: sentence accounting cannot stand in for scope authorization

Evidence: `evaluateStatementSentenceCoverage` removes a sentence from `unmapped` when its normalized text equals either a clause or a `confessions` entry (`verify-ac/clauses.ts`, 1361–1394); `acceptance-resolver.ts` refuses only when `unmappedSentenceCount > 0` (255–260). This is a text-accounting floor. The #4545 addendum describes the separate failure in which an agent-authored implementation decision was treated as permission for backend work despite a UI-only ceiling.

Failure mode: copying the original restriction into `sentences` still lets a worker clear the floor with an agent-authored confession or same-text clause, then cite a passing acceptance walk or generic merge permission as approval to cross the presentation-only boundary. Mapping a sentence is not proof that backend/database work was authorized.

Disposition: keep the restriction binding through dispatch and verification as an authorization ceiling, with explicit actor, affected restriction, and newly allowed change class for amendments. A conflict blocks dependent work; a confession or derived item may report the conflict but cannot amend it. Do not make `verify:ac`'s unmapped count the sole authorization verdict.

### sharpens-framing: compose with the related remedies without declaring this gap dominated

Evidence: [#4545's Bound remedy](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/4545#issuecomment-5837024723) seeds explicit operator scope-limit phrases as a durable ceiling and adds a warn-first untraceable routes/actions/pages list. [#4774's Bound remedy](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/4774#issuecomment-5747186912) addresses changed PR paths against an independent scope baseline. [#4915's terminal record](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/4915#issuecomment-5784448402) closes a persisted AC-deletion leftover as dominated by Wave 2 intent drift plus consumer `soft_empty`. ## Summary

Acceptance checks lose original scope restrictions when an agent rewrites an ingested brief

## Context

An operator authorizes changes to the presentation layer only. The source requirement contains an explicit "view only" restriction. An agent ingests that requirement, derives implementation items, then rewrites the brief's Description and Overview from those derived items.

Observed acceptance behavior: Directive CLI/core 0.119.9. Later delivery checks in the same audited sequence used 0.119.5; these are separate observations, not a claim that one version produced every result. This report describes the observed versions and does not claim a reproduction against the latest upstream revision.

## Expected behavior

The original exclusion must remain part of the acceptance and authorization contract after ingestion, decomposition, narrative cleanup, and dispatch. An agent must not be able to remove an unmet restriction from the material the gate checks and thereby obtain a passing result.

If the source and derived brief disagree, the discrepancy must remain visible and block dependent implementation until the restriction is restored or the operator explicitly authorizes a specific amendment. A rewritten brief, an agent decision, or a generic instruction to continue cannot supply that amendment.

## Actual behavior / gap

1. The source requirement included a presentation-only scope restriction.
2. The initial derived items did not preserve that restriction as a clause.
3. The acceptance sentence-floor check failed and explicitly listed the source restriction among statement sentences that were neither clauses nor confessions.
4. The agent replaced Description and Overview with text assembled from its own derived item titles. That removed the original restriction from those narratives.
5. A subsequent verify:ac invocation returned success. Recorded results included zero verified clauses and nonzero unverifiable clauses.
6. The work proceeded using the rewritten brief as its contract; backend and database work was later performed without an explicit scope amendment.

The gate definition was not edited. The reference text consumed by the gate was weakened. The observed checker extracted statement sentences from the current plan's title, selected narratives, and items; it did not independently compare them with the original source requirement.

The zero-verified result is supporting context, not a claim that the separate rapid-check defect in #4866 is uncorrected. The primary failure here is loss of the original restriction from the acceptance reference.

## Session notes

### Reproduction recipe

This recipe is reconstructed from the observed sequence; it has not been rerun as a separate sanitized fixture.

1. Supply an issue with a useful UI outcome and the explicit restriction "Presentation changes only; do not change persistence or backend processing."
2. Ingest it into a new brief that has no independently preserved source restriction on the merge base.
3. Derive items describing only the positive UI outcomes, leaving the exclusion unmapped.
4. Run verify:ac and retain the failure naming the unmapped restriction.
5. Regenerate Description and Overview solely from those derived item titles, omitting the exclusion. Keep the original source requirement unchanged.
6. Run verify:ac again. A pass obtained because the restriction disappeared from the inspected input reproduces this defect.

### Regression cases

- Deleting an exclusion from Description or Overview must not clear its previous failure.
- Rephrasing, splitting, or moving an exclusion must preserve its meaning and source identity.
- The same protection must apply to a newly ingested brief with no previous brief on the merge base.
- Derived item titles and confessions cannot independently authorize removal of a source restriction.
- An explicit, attributable operator amendment may change the boundary; its affected restriction and resulting scope must be inspectable.
- Acceptance evidence must distinguish an outcome that was verified from one that is merely declared or unverifiable.

### Relationship to existing reports

Refs #4915 for deletion of acceptance prose on persisted briefs, #4545 for enforcement of an explicit operator ceiling, and #977 for source provenance. This report isolates source-to-derived narrowing during initial ingestion and rewriting, including the case where there is no prior brief for a base-versus-head comparison.

The agent's removal of the restriction was a scope violation. This report asks why the independent gate accepted the weakened reference; it does not attribute authorization to the operator.
